chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Sandal, from Yasser, from Al-Yasa' ibn Hamza, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who veils a good deed equals seventy good deeds, and the one who broadcasts an evil deed is rebuked, and the one who veils it is forgiven.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of hiding good deeds versus showing bad ones?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) elucidates the spiritual mechanics of 'satr' (veiling), distinguishing between the voluntary concealment of good deeds to avoid ostentation and the divine mercy in covering sins when one does not publicize them. It underscores the Shia emphasis on sincerity (ikhlas) and humility, where the act of hiding one's piety is rewarded as if it were seventy good deeds, while broadcasting faults invites divine rebuke.
